Building: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (Botta building), San Francisco (museum).
The front (−z) is the Third Street front, across from Yerba Buena Gardens.
Footprint: 108.7 m along x by 84.8 m along z, centred on the origin.
Outline (from OpenStreetMap), [x, z] in metres, going round:
[[-54.3,-42.1],[10.8,-42.4],[10.9,6.5],[54.4,6.4],[54,33.1],[14.6,36.9],[-5.2,37.6],[-5.2,42.4],[-54.4,42.2]]
Height: the highest point is 38 m above the ground.

3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. front elevation of the 1995 Botta building: stepped brick-and-stone masses with the striped cylindrical oculus tower, Snohetta extension rising behind, daylight
  2. corner three-quarter of the Botta brick facade with the cylinder, the white Snohetta extension at left behind, towers beyond
  3. view from the Yerba Buena garden side: stepped brick masses and striped cylinder, extension at right, daylight

Reply with the JSON object only.

json.notes: 1. The striped drum was too plain and too low. The real drum rises above the flanking brick masses, is banded black and white, and carries a striped ring round the glass oculus. Now the drum is 30 m tall, with dark bands and a dark ring and glass disc on the front. 2. The white extension was striped with dark glass bands on every storey. The real lower storey is solid white cladding, with glass bands only on the upper floors, so the lower storey now has no windows. 3. The east wing had the same heavy stripes. It is now solid white below with glass bands only above, and the flanking brick masses rise to 24 m.

The real lower storey is solid white cladding, with glass bands only on the upper floors, so the lower storey now has no windows. 3. The east wing had the same heavy stripes. It is now solid white below with glass bands only above, and the flanking brick masses rise to 24 m.

json.notes: The San Francisco MOMA (Botta) reads as a low brick front, about 12 m high, spanning the full width of the Third Street face, with two taller brick masses flanking a striped drum that carries a glass oculus, centred on the front. Behind and to the east rises the white Snohetta extension, about 38 m high, with horizontal glass bands. The plan's positions hold, except that the flanking brick masses are moved so they sit symmetrically either side of the drum, as in the photographs.
